summary.text: An 85-year-old man from Ivory Coast who frequently traveled to Africa had been followed since 1997 for marginal zone lymphoma with an immunoglobulin M component and translocation (11;18). He had hypertension, Guillain-Barre syndrome and no history of HIV. He received chloraminophene (1997 to 2001) for anemia and medullary involvement, rituximab-cyclophosphamide (2008) after an intestinal recurrence, rituximab-bendamustine (2011) for a gastric relapse, and in 2018 ibrutinib 420 mg orally per day with monthly rituximab for a large mesenteric recurrence.

A CT scan after 6 months of therapy showed the tumour diameter reduced from 9 to 3.5 cm alongside new pulmonary micronodules and mediastino-hilar adenomegalies. He complained of cough and evening fever. Bronchial aspirate culture grew Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex, confirmed by polymerase chain reaction, establishing pulmonary tuberculosis. Neutrophils were 1.15 G/L, lymphocytes 1.1 G/L, with mild hypogammaglobulinemia at 6 g/L.

Rifampycine and isoniazide were given for 6 months, combined with pyrazinamide during the first 2 months. The clinical evolution was satisfactory, with regression of the clinical signs and pulmonary lesions under treatment. During follow-up he developed a Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection that was treated successfully with antibiotics.

No cause is inferred.
